relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with neonatal Alexander disease and a GFAP variant: "In WES analysis, GFAP missense heterozygous variant NM_002055.5: c.1187C>T, p.(Thr396Ile) was detected, confirming the diagnosis of AxD."
method_note: Hand extraction; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from hand-written values. No tables in the paper. In scope: the proband (rule 5 label 'patient'; the paper calls him 'the proband'), his parents (sex not stated, so 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2') and sister, who were tested and did not carry the variant, and one previously published patient carrying the same c.1187C>T variant ([14], PMID:34865968), labelled 'ref [14] patient'. Relatives are described only as 'healthy'; no phenotype rows were made for them and their checklist items are all not reported. For the ref [14] patient, transcript, protein, zygosity, pathogenicity and ACMG were left not reported because they are stated for the proband's finding; age at death 'within the eighth month of life' was not converted to ISO. Several features come from figure legends (medulla signal, midbrain, low signal rim, contrast enhancement). Normal laboratory results at admission (inflammation parameters, ionogram, liver and kidney parameters) were recorded as excluded in the paper's words; later in the course the patient had hyponatremia and high CRP, so these are different time points, not a contradiction. Control CSF showed normalized cytosis and a normal glucose concentration (39 mg/dL), recorded as detail on the observed rows rather than as excluded rows. Differential diagnoses excluded by work-up (lysosomal storage disorders, organic acidurias, aminoacidopathies, fatty acid oxidation defects, GLUT-1 deficiency) are diagnoses, not features, and got no rows. Macrocephaly is marked observed from the title and 'As presented in our patient ... macrocephaly/hydrocephalus'; the paper never gives a head-circumference centile. The paper says the parental result suggests a de novo event while 'germinal mosaicism cannot be excluded'; inheritance recorded as de novo because both parents tested negative.

span: Signs of increased intracranial pressure led to ventriculoperitoneal shunt implantation.

Focal-onset motor seizures with secondary generalization led to the introduction of phenobarbitals. After 3 days, due to recurrent cluster seizures, antiepileptic treatment was modified with levetiracetam.
Suspecting the glucose transporter type 1 (GLUT-1) deficiency syndrome, a ketogenic diet was introduced.
Treatment was modified temporarily with phenytoin and then clobazam, after which a reduction in focal seizures was observed, and then carbamazepine was added.

which were corrected with intravenous (2.2% and 3% NaCl) and oral supplementation (10% NaCl). After an endocrinological consultation, fludrocortisone was implemented. Due to high CRP (99.4 mg/L) values, broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy was used
